items.out: It was the leave to move what was yours, and it was open on Friday. Praise it exactly: not a right the holder could have kept by asking, since it lived on an authority's silence; not a fuse the holder could test by letting it run, since a closure that can be probed is not one that must come as a surprise; not a withdrawn offer or a rival's foreclosure, since no one at the holder's own table decided anything about the holder. It was a permission that could be taken only by a decree on a class, timed for the hours in which the holder could not act. The Greek banks that did not open on Monday 29 June 2015, after a Sunday address, had been open on Friday. The Cypriot bank holiday of March 2013 was extended, after parliament refused the first levy, until the bail-in was law. The Argentine corralito was announced on a Saturday in December 2001. The export licence was suspended and the delisting published after the fact. What ran the clock was the authority's own calendar, laid across the Friday night and the bank holiday so that the announcement and the shutting were one act, because the announcement would have been the signal to exercise, and the closure worked only unannounced. This is what it was: the one expiry on the map whose notice could not precede it. There was a last act that would have kept it, and it was ugly: a transfer made on rumour, paid for in the chance of being wrong and in the discount the rumour market charges; the deposits that left Greece that spring left on nothing better. The holder who waited for a date was waiting for a thing the mechanism forbade, and knows it now. What remains is the entry it leaves beside runway-illusions' Cash behind glass, which counts the deposit taken into receivership on a Friday as owned and unreachable; this was the mechanism that chose the Friday. It was closed by name and not as a side effect, and the item stands on that fence.

items.out: It was the standing to be paid, or to sue in one's own name, and it was the holder's right up to a date the holder never saw. Name what it was: a permission, whole and good, that ended on a day fixed in a proceeding the holder was not attending, by a rule that deemed the holder to have read the notice. The bankruptcy court's bar date for proofs of claim, noticed to unknown creditors by publication. The class settlement whose opt-out date came on a postcard that looked like advertising. The probate creditor's window, once the notice had run in the county paper. Its clock was the bar-date order joined to the rule of constructive notice, under which publication counts as knowledge for anyone the debtor could not name. And the act that would have kept it was the smallest in the law: a one-page proof of claim, a signed opt-out, the cheapest filing there is and the one least often made, because the holder who would have made it was, by construction, the one who was not told. Nothing was missing from the record; only the holder was missing from the room, which is why this was never deal-deaths' Missing witness. What it leaves behind is a line beside runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, where the permission carries a date the holder can read on the stamp: this was the date written on someone else's docket and imputed to the holder. That is what it was, and it was the holder's, and it is done.

items.out: It was a permission, and it carried no date of its own; that was its whole nature and its whole fault. It was granted under a parent instrument that had a term, and when the parent ended it ended too, on its merits or against them, with nothing printed on its face to say so. The emergency-use authorization that ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, which is a different paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations standing. The cross-state telehealth licence that lapsed with each state's emergency through 2021 and 2022. The wartime power. The pilot programme run under a waiver. The sub-lease that died with the head lease. What ran its clock was the parent's date, which the holder never signed and may never have read, since the grant the holder did read carried none, and the holder first had to find which parent paper carried it. There was a way to keep it, and it deserves naming: conversion. A full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in one's own name, filed while the parent still stood. The conversion was slow enough that it had to be started while the emergency looked endless, which is exactly the season in which nobody starts it. It was not Bar date in the newspaper, whose date sits on a docket and is imputed; here the date was on a different paper than the option and was honest. It was not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait the rule imposes; this rule did not wait, it ended. It was an honest permission with an honest parent, and it went when the parent went.

items.out: It was a capability, the cortex's willingness to rewire, and it belonged to a child who did not know there was an eye to save. Say exactly what it was: an option that expired by the holder's own development, on a schedule the holder could not know, so that the last act that could keep it was necessarily in another hand. Amblyopia is most correctable by patching the good eye in the first years and responds less, and less completely, after about seven, though the trials of the 2000s found response into the early teens. The clubfoot cast in infancy. The second language spoken without an accent, which is contested as a hard window. The duckling that imprints in its first day. Its clock was the developmental timetable, and nothing the child did or left undone ran it, which is why it was never a use-it-or-lose-it. What could have kept it was a screening: the preschool vision check, the parent who noticed a squint. The option belonged to one person and its preservation to another, and where no screening programme existed it expired unseen, at a rate that was a property of the programme and not of the child. Beside Last known well, where a witness dates the option, this was the case in which the holder could not be its own witness at all. It was a window that closed on a child who never knew it was open, and the eye it would have saved is the measure of it.

items.out: It was a treatment the body might still have allowed. Name it exactly: a capability, dated not by the fact but by the last witness to the fact, so that it expired when the proof ran out while the tissue might still have taken the drug. The stroke patient who woke with the deficit was ineligible for thrombolysis because the four-and-a-half-hour window was counted from when she was last seen well, which was bedtime, so the wake-up stroke lost the drug regardless of when the artery closed. The same rule dated the opened vial with no time written on the label and the sample whose chain of custody had a gap, both treated as expired at the earliest hour they could have been. What ran its clock was the protocol's timestamp rule, which asked for a witness and not for the tissue. What would have kept it was a witness: someone awake, a time written on the vial, or a witness of another kind, the imaging that reads the tissue's own clock, by which the WAKE-UP trial of 2018 returned the drug to patients with no witnessed onset. This was not Patch before seven, where the body's own clock had run; here the body's clock may not have run at all, and the record's had. Beside witness-architectures, which asks what must exist for a trace to form, this was the option that died for want of a trace while the fact would still have allowed it. It was good until the paper said it was not, and the paper was all anyone could read.

items.out: It was the justiciability of a claim, a permission to be decided, and it ended with no one declining and no one ruling. Name it: the situation resolved itself faster than the forum that would have decided it could move. The student whose challenge to a law school's admissions was dismissed as moot because he was about to graduate (DeFunis, 1974). The pregnancy over before the appeal. The election held before the ballot-access case. The tenant evicted before the housing court sat. The employee whose grievance was mooted by the reorganization that abolished the post. What ran its clock was a ratio, the forum's pace against the harm's duration, and no party at the table set that number. Nothing was eaten on a curve, so this was never deal-deaths' Cost of the last mile; the harm was simply over. There was no date anywhere, so it was never Bar date in the newspaper. And the way it could have been kept deserves its full name: a structure that outlived the individual harm. The class certified before the named plaintiff's harm ended, which is what Sosna (1975) allowed; or the doctrine that a harm capable of repetition yet evading review may be decided anyway, which is what Roe rested on. It was kept, when it was kept, by a coordination or by a rule and never by hurrying. It was a question that was real, and it ended unanswered because the world finished first.

items.out: It was a counterparty: the specific body whose yes was available, and it was there, and then its term ended with the matter pending, and its successor never had to say no. Name what was lost exactly: the matter's place in the process, since the successor started it at zero. The bills that died on adjournment sine die and had to be reintroduced from the beginning. The treaty signed and awaiting a parliament that was dissolved. The permit application before a council that was re-elected. The approval the old board agreed in the hallway and had not yet minuted when the board was reconstituted at the meeting. The offer approved by a committee disbanded in the reorganization. What ran its clock was the ratifier's own calendar, election, session, or term. What would have kept it: the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in the hallway. Say honestly that the treaty cases are simplified, since most unratified treaties were eventually refused by someone; the clean form is the legislative bill, which dies by the thousand each session with no recorded no. This was not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by transfer; here it was replaced by the calendar. Beside deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal, where the ratifier wanted a different bargain, stands this: the ratifier that wanted this one and was gone before the vote. That is what it was. It wanted to say yes.

items.out: It was a counterparty, the one whose word held the option, and the word was good while the person stayed. Name exactly what it was: an option held in a person rather than on the paper that transfers, so it ended at the counterparty's next transfer, which the holder did not control and often did not see. The renewal promised by the landlord who sold the building to a buyer not bound by unrecorded promises. The 'we'll take you back' from a manager who left. The side letter with a fund's partner that the fund's successor manager had never seen. The supplier's verbal priority that vanished with the account executive. What ran its clock was the register, the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, the paper on which the option was never written, so the successor took free of it. What would have kept it was recording: a memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise put on the paper that binds successors, at the cost of the awkwardness of asking a friendly counterparty to bind their unknown replacement. This was not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes; here the shape stayed and the counterparty went. Beside term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair, where the replacement exercises a term the friend would not have, stands its mirror: the replacement who declined to honour a term the friend gave. It was a promise, and it was kept by the one who made it, for as long as that one was there.

items.out: It was a shape that could receive the holder: a capability on the counterparty's side, a vacancy nobody had yet re-planned. Name it exactly: the option to return, and it ended at the counterparty's next planning cycle without anyone declining the return. The leave taken with no return date whose post was redistributed among three people at the next reorganization. The budget line reallocated at year end. The supplier's line retooled for the customer who stayed. The co-founder's seat that the remaining founders stopped leaving empty at the next hire. What was lost was the return to the seat; employment there afterwards is a new negotiation from the outside. What ran its clock was the counterparty's planning cadence, quarterly, annual, the next reorganization, which set the expiry without reference to the holder at all. What would have kept it was a dated return, a leave rather than a resignation, a reservation the cycle had to respect, or the return itself before the cycle turned. No one opposed the return, which is what sets this beside traces-of-the-unlived's Vacancy tenant, where preparation for a future breeds its opponents; here the absence was simply absorbed. And it was not forms-of-return's Reentry burn, a road open and hostile one way; this road closed. It was an empty chair kept empty by nobody's decision, and it filled the same way.

items.out: It was a coordination, a set of yeses that would have been enough together, and it ended because the gathering did not outrun the decay of each yes. Name it exactly: an option that required many simultaneous assents, so that it had a half-life. The recall petition whose signatures older than sixty days are invalid under Michigan's rule, or that must all fall within California's hundred and sixty days. The tender offer's minimum condition that had to be met by the offer's expiry. The crowd in the square that went home. The reunion that became impossible one death at a time. What ran its clock was the validity window on each act of assent, written by the rule or by the assenter's own attention. What would have kept it was a gathering rate: paid circulators, a date agreed in advance, a pact that bound the early yeses until the last arrived. Say plainly that the recall and tender cases are observed and the crowd is analogy. This was not Session ends, where one body's calendar kills the matter; here many small calendars did. Beside who-can-be-bound's Place in line, an ordering lost by leaving, stands this, the coordination lost by others' leaving. Every yes in it was real, and each was given, and each was gone before the last.

items.out: It was a counterparty, the buyer whose capacity was the option, and it was the holder's own growth that moved it out of reach. Name exactly what it was: the option to sell to the natural acquirer, which ended at the round that priced the company above what the acquirer could pay at all, a market capitalization smaller than the price, a wage cap, a fund's concentration limit, and past those a board's approval ceiling, with nobody at either table declining. The company whose preference stack came to exceed the largest deal its three strategic buyers had ever done. The player whose wage outgrew every club in the league but two. The practice too large for any partner to buy in and too small to be listed. What ran its clock was the acquirer's capacity, readable in its market value and its deal history, set against the holder's own price, which each round raised. What would have kept it was the sale at the last price under the ceiling, which was never seen as the last, or a round sized to stay under it, which is the one choice a founder is never advised to make. Say honestly that this is analytical: every observed case can be read as a buyer that would have paid more, so it stands as a mechanism and not a count. It was a door exactly the holder's size, and the holder grew.

items.out: It was a permission, about to be withdrawn by a third party's rule change, and it could be kept only by an act in the world that no paper substituted for. What ran its clock was the code and the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, as in Washington, on a complete application, so the last act differed by jurisdiction, and the holder who knew which had a different week. What would have kept it was the hole in the ground before the vote, an exercise begun rather than a filing made; the option could be preserved only by starting to use it. items.out: It was a permission that lived only while it was used, and it ended by disuse. Name exactly what it was: a right whose clock ran while the holder did nothing and stopped when the holder acted, and whose preserving act was the exercise emptied of its purpose. The airport slot that had to be flown eighty percent of the season or returned, which had airlines flying empty aircraft in early 2020 until the rule was waived. The water right under prior appropriation, forfeited after five years without beneficial use, which has fields irrigated in a drought to keep them. The trade mark abandoned after three years' non-use. The mining claim kept by annual labour. The department budget spent in the last quarter so that it is not cut. What ran its clock was the regulator's usage ledger. What would have kept it was the empty flight, which cost the whole price of using the option and returned nothing but the option, so that keeping and using were the same act and the option's upkeep was its exercise price. It was not Pour the foundation, one act that vests; here no act ever finished the keeping. Beside runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, whose licence lapses without hours logged and whose clock no cash extends, stands the price at which it could be extended after all: the hours flown for nobody.
